name: TSHA-102
summary: TSHA-102 is Taysha's self-complementary AAV9 gene therapy carrying a MECP2 minigene under miRARE auto-regulation, given once by lumbar intrathecal injection (1x10^15 total vg) for Rett syndrome. The registrational study is the REVEAL pivotal trial (Part B of NCT05606614): single-arm and open-label in 17 females aged 6 to <22 in the developmental plateau population with a MECP2 loss-of-function mutation. The primary endpoint is the share who gain or regain at least one of 28 natural-history milestones, with 33% the success bar against a 6.7% null. Dosing finished in June 2026, and a 6-month interim is the planned BLA basis, with topline data and FDA feedback in 1H 2027. ASPIRE (NCT07480564, 4 girls aged 2 to <4) supplies safety for a planned label of age 2 and over (8-K 0001193125-26-344594). Price anchor: Itvisma, Novartis's one-time intrathecal AAV9 therapy for SMA from age 2 into adulthood, at its $2.59mm WAC, less the 0.36 Zolgensma discount the book's NTLA-2002 seed measured. Net is $1.658mm a course. Uptake anchor: Daybue, the only approved Rett therapy. More than 1,500 US patients had started it by October 2024, 18 months after launch: 25.3% of the 5,940 female Rett patients counted in US claims. TSHA-102 is set to treat the same share of its eligible pool by the end of year five, which peaks at 483 patients and about $801mm US net in 2032. Taysha holds unencumbered rights since Astellas's option lapsed in October 2025. It pays Abeona a high single-digit royalty, netted at 7% over Alnylam's 0.1363 margin (the book's cost-block proxy for rare-disease genetic medicine companies), so Taysha keeps 0.486427 of the asset.

therapy_mode.source: Taysha 8-K 2026-08-11 (0001193125-26-344594, EX-99.1): 'Designed as a one-time treatment, TSHA-102 aims to address the genetic root cause of the disease'; the REVEAL pivotal trial evaluates 'a single intrathecal (IT) administration of high dose TSHA-102 (1x10 15 total vector genomes (vg))'. Same wording in the 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-344610): 'a single lumbar intrathecal administration'
therapy_mode.note: One dose, not repeated, so each year's treated patients are that year's revenue. The book models its other one-time gene and gene-editing therapies the same way (NTLA-2002; the Casgevy seed)
therapy_mode.check: Read in the book's filing_sections. 8-K 0001193125-26-344594 EX-99.1 (2026-08-11), 'About TSHA-102': 'Designed as a one-time treatment, TSHA-102 aims to address the genetic root cause of the disease'; REVEAL pivotal evaluates 'a single intrathecal (IT) administration of high dose TSHA-102 (1x10 15 total vector genomes (vg))'. 10-Q 0001193125-26-344610: 'a single lumbar intrathecal administration in females aged 6 to <22 years'. One dose, not repeated, so one_time is right and matches the NTLA-2002 seed.

list_price_per_patient.unit: mm USD per course (one intrathecal dose)
list_price_per_patient.source: Itvisma (onasemnogene abeparvovec-brve), Novartis's intrathecal AAV9 gene therapy for SMA: 'Novartis is pricing the one-time intrathecal gene therapy at a wholesale acquisition cost of $2.59 million' (Fierce Pharma, 'Novartis scores FDA approval for new version of SMA gene therapy, prices at $2.59M', fiercepharma.com/pharma/novartis-scores-fda-approval-new-version-sma-gene-therapy-prices-259m; Managed Healthcare Executive, 'FDA approves $2.59 million gene therapy for SMA'). Label per the Novartis US release: 'children two years and older, teens, and adults living with SMA with a confirmed mutation in the SMN1 gene', a one-time fixed dose given intrathecally (novartis.com/us-en/news/media-releases/novartis-receives-fda-approval-itvisma-only-gene-replacement-therapy-children-two-years-and-older-teens-and-adults-spinal-muscular-atrophy-sma). All read from the search summary; pages not opened
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the anchor. Taysha has set no price. Its payer research found TSHA-102 'viewed as a high-value therapy due to its transformative disease-modifying potential', with durability 'the key value determinant' (8-K 0001193125-26-344594). Itvisma is the closest priced product: the same capsid (AAV9), route (intrathecal, outpatient) and one fixed dose, a label from age 2 into adulthood, and a monogenic CNS disease. Zolgensma, the IV version for SMA under age 2, lists at $2.125mm (as the book's NTLA-2002 seed carries it, from BioSpace). Cross-check against the Rett incumbent: Daybue earned $391mm net in FY2025 (Acadia FY2025 results release, search summary) on 954 to 987 US patients a quarter in Q1 and Q2 2025 (Acadia Q1 and Q2 2025 releases, search summary). That is about $396,000 net per patient-year, so TSHA-102's $1.658mm net is about 4.2 years of Daybue. Case for higher: Rett has no disease-modifying therapy, a one-time dose replaces lifelong symptomatic care, all 12 REVEAL Part A patients gained at least one milestone by 12 months (8-K 0001193125-26-276738), and 4.2 years of the incumbent is a low multiple by the one-time-therapy pricing logic payers use. Case for lower: the evidence is one single-arm trial of 17 patients against natural history, durability is shown only to 30 months, and Rett is not fatal in infancy as SMA type 1 is, so the cost-offset case is weaker than Zolgensma's. Payers told Taysha that 'strong efficacy, safety and durability are expected to drive coverage'. At Zolgensma's $2.125mm, net would be $1.36mm
list_price_per_patient.check: WebSearch: Fierce Pharma ('Novartis scores FDA approval for new version of SMA gene therapy, prices at $2.59M'), Managed Healthcare Executive ('FDA approves $2.59 million gene therapy for SMA') and a Reuters brief (sahmcapital.com, 2025-11-25, 'Novartis Prices Itvisma At A Wholesale Acquisition Cost Of $2.59 Million') all give a $2.59mm WAC for the one-time intrathecal therapy; Novartis says it costs 35% to 46% less than chronic SMA treatment over 10 years. Label read in the book (labels table, asset 429, SPL effective 2026-06-29): 'ITVISMA is indicated for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with confirmed mutation in survival motor neuron 1 (SMN1) gene'; NVS 20-F 0001114448-26-000004: 'an intrathecal injection (Itvisma)'. Same capsid, route, one fixed dose and a from-age-2 label as TSHA-102's plan, so the anchor fits. Zolgensma's $2.125mm confirmed by BioSpace's approval headline. Unit: mm USD per course, the book's one-time convention (NTLA-2002 carries 2.2 per course). Cross-checks: Daybue FY2025 net sales $391mm and 987 unique US patients shipped in Q2 2025 (Acadia releases, via search) give about $396,000 per patient-year, so $1.658mm net is 4.2 years, as stated. Novartis's own logic (35% to 46% below ten years of the chronic comparator) applied to Daybue's ~$396,000 gives $2.14mm to $2.57mm, just under $2.59mm, which supports the anchor within a narrow band. Judgement labelled, with case each way.

gross_to_net_pct.source: Zolgensma (onasemnogene abeparvovec, one-time IV AAV9): CMS reimbursement had fallen to $1.36mm per claim by 2022 against a $2.125mm list, 'nearly a 40% discount' (BioSpace, 'Who's Paying for Million-Dollar Gene Therapies?', biospace.com/who-s-paying-for-million-dollar-gene-therapies). 1 - 1.36/2.125 = 0.36. Carried unchanged from the book's second-read NTLA-2002 seed (verified/NTLA_biological_ntla_2002.json, gross_to_net_pct, verdict confirmed)
gross_to_net_pct.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator, kept consistent with the NTLA-2002 seed. The anchor is a published WAC, so neither Medicare convention applies and the discount must be sourced. Zolgensma is the same molecule family and maker as the Itvisma anchor, and the one one-time AAV9 therapy with a measured net-to-list figure. Direction checked: 0.36 comes off list, so net = 2.59 x 0.64 = $1.658mm a course. Case for lower: the book's Casgevy seed assumes about 18%, and the Medicaid statutory rebate (23.1% of AMP) reaches Medicaid units only. Case for higher: if $1.36mm is CMS's Part B limit (106% of ASP), the ASP-based discount is 0.396. The Rett payer mix is not sourced here, and it decides which of these fits
gross_to_net_pct.check: WebSearch of BioSpace 'Who's Paying for Million-Dollar Gene Therapies?': 'public insurers paid $1.89 million per claim in 2019, and by 2022, that figure dropped to $1.36 million, nearly a 40% discount from its list price, according to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services'; CMS spent about $87.25mm on some 63 treatments; Medicaid covers over half of children with SMA. 1 - 1.36/2.125 = 0.36 exactly; direction right (share off list), net 2.59 x 0.64 = $1.6576mm. Same value as the confirmed NTLA-2002 seed (verified/NTLA_biological_ntla_2002.json). DOES THE BASIS TRANSFER: the measurement is a public-payer (mostly Medicaid) per-claim payment for the same molecule from the same maker, a one-time AAV9 dose; Itvisma's own net is not disclosed (Novartis reports it only inside 'Zolgensma Group', USD 365mm in Q2 2026, 6-K 0001114448-26-000012), so Zolgensma is the only measured basis. It fits Rett at least as well as HAE: Rett patients are lifelong-dependent and a pediatric-heavy pool, closer to SMA's Medicaid-weighted mix. A search for Daybue's payer mix returned nothing, so the Rett mix stays unsourced, as the note says. The note's case for higher (0.396 if $1.36mm is 106% of ASP) and lower (Casgevy's ~18%) stand. Labelled judgement; inputs confirmed.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.note: Inert in one_time mode, and set so a switch to chronic would carry no treated stock forward. Re-dosing is not modelled
discontinuation_pct.check: One intrathecal dose, not repeated (8-K 0001193125-26-344594, read in the book). In forecast.py the one_time branch bills each year's new patients once and reads discontinuation_pct only in the chronic branch, so 1.0 is inert and matches the NTLA-2002 seed.

cogs_per_patient.source: none filed. Taysha's FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-115202), 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-344610) and 8-Ks through 2026-08-11 in the book's filing_sections give no cost of goods or per-course manufacturing cost. They describe the expanded Catalent commercial supply agreement (Harmans, Maryland) without its prices
cogs_per_patient.note: Left null. Taysha has no product revenue, so no cost-of-sales ratio exists either. WARNING for the company step: in one_time mode the engine charges cogs_pct x revenue when this field is null, and Taysha has no company rows in the book, so unless that step sets cogs_pct the build charges no cost of goods at all. AAV manufacture at 1x10^15 vg a dose is costly, so a proxy should come from a gene therapy seller rather than an antibody company
cogs_per_patient.check: Null holds. A regex over all 24 TSHA filing_sections in the book (10-K 0001193125-26-115202, both 2026 10-Qs, 8-Ks to 2026-08-11) finds no 'cost of goods', 'cost of sales', 'cost of revenue', 'gross margin' or per-dose cost; 'manufacturing costs' appears only as an R&D expense component. The Catalent supply agreement is described without prices. The note's WARNING is now resolved by the company step: Taysha's cost block borrows Alnylam's rows (cogs_pct 0.1823, sga 0.326, rd 0.3554, other 0; the same comparator the NTLA-2002, DYNE-101, DYNE-251 and deramiocel seeds carry in er_tool.db assumptions), so in one_time mode the engine charges 18.23% of revenue as cost of goods. That is below what AAV at 1x10^15 vg likely costs, a case for a lower margin, but no filed figure exists.

forecast_start_year.source: 8-K 2026-08-11 (0001193125-26-344594, EX-99.1): 'Topline data from REVEAL pivotal trial 6-month interim analysis and FDA feedback on the BLA submission pathway for TSHA-102 is expected in the first half of 2027'; PPQ campaign completes in Q4 2026; cash runway 'into the second half of 2028 and through potential BLA approval of TSHA-102'. 10-Q Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-344610): the interim follows once all 17 patients complete six months, and 'the FDA has agreed that our clinical and final commercial manufacturing processes are considered comparable'. NCT05606614 primary completion 2031-06, estimated (book trials table, last update 2026-07-07). That date spans the whole Phase 1/2/3 with long-term follow-up and is not the BLA date. Amass TrialCore was unavailable (usage limit)
forecast_start_year.note: JUDGEMENT. A 2027 launch is unlikely because Taysha will only discuss the BLA pathway with the FDA in 1H 2027, so submission comes after that. With Breakthrough, RMAT, Fast Track and rare pediatric disease designations (8-K 0001193125-26-344594), a priority review of about 8 months from submission puts approval in 2028. That fits the runway Taysha guides to 'through potential BLA approval' in 2H 2028. 2028 is a partial launch year, and the ramp starts at 8.5% of peak in year 0. Case for 2029: the FDA may want 12-month data or more patients from a 17-patient single-arm study, and it may call an advisory committee or raise CMC review questions on a new commercial site. Case for 2027: third-party commentary (BioEquity Watch on Substack, via search) expects approval in 2027. No filing supports a 2027 submission and approval
forecast_start_year.check: Read in the book. 10-Q 0001193125-26-344610 and 8-K 0001193125-26-344594: dosing of all 17 REVEAL pivotal patients complete (June 2026); 'The interim analysis ... is expected to occur after all 17 patients complete six months of post-treatment follow-up', then 'we plan to discuss data from the 6-month interim analysis and next steps toward the BLA submission pathway with the FDA, with topline data and regulatory feedback anticipated in the first half of 2027'; PPQ 'initiated ... in April 2026 and expect to complete the campaign in the fourth quarter of 2026'; FDA agreed clinical and commercial processes are comparable; runway 'into the second half of 2028 and through potential BLA approval'. Designations confirmed (Breakthrough, RMAT, Fast Track, Orphan, Rare Pediatric Disease). NEW FILED EVIDENCE that supports 2028: the 2025 Trinity term loan (10-Q note) makes Tranche B available 'until March 31, 2028' on BLA submission and Tranche C 'until March 31, 2029' on BLA approval, so the lender window assumes submission by Q1 2028 and approval by Q1 2029. Submission in 2H 2027 plus an 8-month priority review puts approval in 2028. 2028 is the launch year (partial), the book's convention for a launch clearly after the first full year (DYNE-101 seed). Search found no later Taysha timing update. Amass TrialCore was out of quota; NCT05606614 primary completion 2031-06 (estimated) confirmed in the book's trials table, and it is not the BLA gate. Case for 2029 stands (Tranche C's window runs to March 2029).

exus_multiple.source: Taysha FY2025 10-K risk factors (0001193125-26-115202): 'we expect to build a focused sales and marketing infrastructure to market some of our product candidates in the United States'. No ex-US filing, partner or launch timing is disclosed in the 10-K, the 2026 10-Qs or the 2026 8-Ks. The EU orphan designation and UK ILAP designation are the only ex-US steps (8-K 0001193125-26-344594)
exus_multiple.note: Null, so no ex-US revenue is modelled. The filed comparators bracket it but neither fits. Case for higher: Zolgensma, the one-time AAV9 comparator, sold $413mm US and $819mm rest of world in FY2025 (book asset_revenue_regions, NVS 20-F 0001114448-26-000004), 1.98x. It is sold by a global pharma, though, and much of it goes to infants treated at incidence in newly covered markets. Taysha puts its addressable MECP2 population at 15,000 to 20,000 across the US, EU and UK against 6,000 to 9,000 in the US (10-K). Case for near zero: the Rett incumbent Daybue, from a small US company, sells outside North America only through named-patient supply and Canada, with no filed split (Acadia FY2025 10-K and releases, search summary). Set it once Taysha files an ex-US plan or partner
exus_multiple.check: Null holds. 10-K 0001193125-26-115202 risk factors (read in the book): 'we expect to build a focused sales and marketing infrastructure to market some of our product candidates in the United States, if and when they are approved'. No ex-US filing, partner or launch plan appears in the 10-K, 2026 10-Qs or 8-Ks; the only ex-US steps are EC orphan designation and MHRA ILAP (8-K 0001193125-26-344594). The Zolgensma split cited as the case for higher is confirmed in the book (asset_revenue_regions, asset 404, FY2025: US $413mm, rest of world $819mm, 1.98x, NVS 20-F 0001114448-26-000004). The 10-K's 15,000 to 20,000 US+EU+UK against 6,000 to 9,000 US is confirmed.

economics_share.source: Taysha FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-115202), MD&A 'License Agreements' and financial statement note, repeated in the Q2 2026 10-Q (0001193125-26-344610), all read in the book's filing_sections. Abeona Rett Agreement (October 2020): 'exclusive, worldwide, royalty-bearing license' to UNC, University of Edinburgh and Abeona patents, know-how and materials; 'We are obligated to pay Abeona up to $26.5 million in regulatory-related milestones and up to $30.0 million in sales-related milestones per licensed product and high single-digit royalties on net sales of licensed products', payable to the latest of last licensed patent expiry, loss of exclusivity, or ten years from first sale. UT Southwestern: 'exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license' and 'We do not have any future milestone or royalty obligations to UT Southwestern under the UT Southwestern Agreement, other than costs related to the maintenance of patents'. Astellas: 'In October 2025, the Rett Option expired without being exercised ... we now hold unencumbered rights to the TSHA-102 program'. Netted as the book nets a royalty the company pays: (margin - royalty) / margin. Margin from Alnylam's FY2025 cost rows, the book's comparator for rare-disease genetic medicine companies without cost lines of their own (er_tool.db assumptions on the NTLA-2002, DYNE-101, DYNE-251 and deramiocel seeds: cogs 0.1823, sga 0.326, rd 0.3554, other_costs 0.0, 'ALNY FY2025, computed from the filed lines'), 1 - 0.8637 = 0.1363. (0.1363 - 0.07) / 0.1363 = 0.486427
economics_share.note: JUDGEMENT twice, and PROVISIONAL. (1) Tier: 'high single-digit' is taken at its bottom, 7%, as the disitamab vedotin, NBI-1117568 and telitacicept seeds read the same wording. (2) Margin: Taysha is pre-revenue and its company rows borrow Alnylam's filed FY2025 lines, as the Intellia, Dyne and Capricor seeds do; re-strike as (m - 0.07) / m if Taysha's block changes. Case for higher: Alnylam's 0.1363 is its first year of profit, and at a 0.20 margin the share is 0.65, at 0.30 it is 0.7667. Case for lower: at 8% the share is 0.4131 and at 9%, the top of high single digits, 0.3397; an AAV's cost of goods is likely above Alnylam's 18.2%, which thins the margin further. The only other licence on TSHA-102 (UT Southwestern, the MECP2 minigene vector patents) is royalty-free, so no royalty goes unnetted, and REGENX's AAV9 capsid patents expire in 2026 (10-K), before launch. Not netted, as in the book's other royalty seeds: $7.5mm of Abeona milestones already triggered ($1.0mm in 2022, $3.5mm in 2023, $3.0mm in December 2025, paid January 2026), the unstated remainder of the $26.5mm regulatory total, and up to $30.0mm of sales milestones
economics_share.check: 0.700214 -> 0.486427. Royalty wording confirmed verbatim in the book's filing_sections: FY2025 10-K 0001193125-26-115202 MD&A and notes, and Q2 2026 10-Q 0001193125-26-344610 note ('high single-digit royalties on net sales of licensed Rett products'). No rate beyond the tier is filed; the book reads 'high single digit' at 7% (verified disitamab vedotin, NBI-1117568 and telitacicept seeds). OTHER ROYALTIES: UT Southwestern is royalty-free with no future milestone or royalty obligations beyond patent maintenance (10-K MD&A and notes), so it needs no rate and does not trigger a refusal; the Abeona CLN1 licence was terminated in February 2026 and covers CLN1 only; the Astellas option expired unexercised in October 2025. No other royalty wording in any TSHA filing in the book. CORRECTION: the researcher netted over argenx's margin (0.2335, copied from the telitacicept seed). The book's convention for rare-disease genetic medicine companies is Alnylam's rows (er_tool.db assumptions: NTLA-2002, DYNE-101, DYNE-251, deramiocel all carry cogs 0.1823, sga 0.326, rd 0.3554, other 0.0 from 'ALNY FY2025, computed from the filed lines'). Margin 1 - 0.1823 - 0.326 - 0.3554 - 0 = 0.1363; (0.1363 - 0.07) / 0.1363 = 0.486427. On the unrounded Alnylam lines (0.182331, 0.325992, 0.355357; margin 0.13632) it is 0.486502, immaterial. Sensitivities recomputed: 8% 0.4131, 9% 0.3397.

prevalence.source: May D et al., 'Epidemiology and patient journey of Rett syndrome in the United States: a real-world evidence study', BMC Neurol 2023;23:141, doi:10.1186/s12883-023-03181-y (PMID 37016355, PMC10071755). IQVIA Dx and LRx claims, 11/2016 to 10/2019: '5,940 female patients' with at least one medical claim coded Rett (ICD-10-CM F84.2), 3,078 under 18 and 2,862 aged 18 or over, mean age 20.0. Male patients were excluded 'because of uncertainty in correctly identifying these patients'
prevalence.note: Not carried by the book: lookup.py pool 'Rett' returns nothing, epidemiology.csv has no Rett line, and there are no Daybue demand rows or trofinetide seeds. This is the first Rett pool, and later Rett seeds should reuse it. WHICH FIGURE AND WHY: 5,940, a measured count of diagnosed female patients, with its method in print. Not 7,500, the midpoint of the 6,000 to 9,000 that Acadia and Taysha give for everyone in the US with Rett. Taysha's 10-K (0001193125-26-115202) puts it as 'patient estimates range from 6,000 to 9,000 based on claims data and epidemiology data', and that range includes the undiagnosed, whom a gene therapy needing a diagnosis and a MECP2 test cannot reach. Not 4,500 either: Acadia's stated 'diagnosed population of approximately 4,500 U.S. patients' (search summary), which it publishes without a method. JUDGEMENT to take the claims count. Case for higher: it is one database's three-year cohort, not a national projection, and captures only patients seen at least once. Its own female prevalence of 0.45 to 0.52 per 10,000 female enrollees implies more nationally. Case for lower: one F84.2 code in any position qualified, 16.2% had a different diagnosis first, and genetic testing was observed before the index claim in only 1.2%. Some coded patients may not have Rett, which Acadia's 4,500 would reflect
prevalence.check: PubMed PMID 37016355 (May D et al., BMC Neurol 2023;23:141, doi:10.1186/s12883-023-03181-y, PMC10071755), full text read: 'There were 5,940 female patients included in the study population after all eligibility criteria were applied; 3,078 (52%) comprised the pediatric cohort and 2,862 (48%) comprised the adult cohort'; IQVIA Dx and LRx, 11/1/2016 to 10/31/2019, at least one F84.2 claim in any position; males excluded for uncertain identification; female annual prevalence 0.45 to 0.52 per 10,000; genetic testing before index 1.2%; 16.2% with a prior differential diagnosis. All as stated. lookup.py pool Rett returns nothing and epidemiology.csv has no Rett line, so the book does not carry it. Two points the note does not make: (a) the databases cover 'over 130 million beneficiaries', and the count is patients seen over three years, so it is neither a national projection nor a point prevalence; the paper's own female rate scaled nationally would be higher, as the note's case for higher says. (b) The note calls Taysha's 6,000 to 9,000 a count of 'everyone in the US with Rett', but the 10-K frames it as the US part of 'the estimated addressable patient population with typical Rett syndrome caused by a pathogenic/likely pathogenic MECP2 mutation'. That range is already MECP2-positive, so the 5,453 eligible here sit below its floor, which strengthens the case for higher. The value is a labelled judgement with its source confirmed.

incidence.source: Laurvick CL et al., 'Rett syndrome in Australia: a review of the epidemiology', J Pediatr 2006;148(3):347-52, doi:10.1016/j.jpeds.2005.10.037 (PMID 16615965): 'cumulative incidence was 1.09 per 10,000 females by 12 years of age'. May 2023 (PMID 37016355) uses 'an estimated incidence of 1 in 10,000 females by the age of 12 in the United States'. US female births in 2024: 3,628,934 births (NVSR Births: Final Data for 2024, as the book's MMRVNS and PCV21 seeds carry it) less the 1,854,394 male births the book's deramiocel seed derives at 1,045 males per 1,000 = 1,774,540. x 1.09 / 10,000 = 193.4
incidence.note: JUDGEMENT. Rett is almost entirely de novo, so the inflow is demographic: each female birth cohort is assumed to reach diagnosis at Laurvick's rate. The book's HAE and DMD seeds use the same method. Not the claims incidence in May 2023 (0.31 per 10,000 female enrollees in 2019), which counts prevalent patients newly seen in the database as new, as its authors note. Taysha's '1 of every 8,700 female births' would give 204. The engine filters the inflow by eligible_pct: 193 x 0.918084 = 177 a year
incidence.check: PubMed PMID 16615965 (Laurvick CL et al., J Pediatr 2006;148(3):347-52, doi:10.1016/j.jpeds.2005.10.037) abstract: 'the cumulative incidence was 1.09 per 10,000 females by 12 years of age'. May 2023 full text: 'an estimated incidence of 1 in 10,000 females by the age of 12 in the United States'. Female births recomputed: 3,628,934 (the 2024 NVSR total the verified MMRVNS and varicella seeds carry) x 1,000/2,045 = 1,774,540 (males 1,854,394, as the verified deramiocel seed carries); x 1.09 / 10,000 = 193.4. Taysha's '1 of every 8,700 female births worldwide' is confirmed in 8-K 0001193125-26-276738 exhibit 2 and gives 204. May 2023's female claims incidence of 0.31 per 10,000 in 2019 and its note that adult 'incident' cases may be misclassified are confirmed. Engine inflow 193 x 0.918084 = 177.2. Labelled judgement.

eligible_pct.source: Label population as filed: Taysha plans 'broad labeling of TSHA-102 for patients aged ≥2 years with Rett syndrome' (10-K 0001193125-26-115202; 10-Q 0001193125-26-344610). REVEAL enrols 'females aged 6 to <22 years with Rett syndrome due to MECP2 loss-of-function mutation' in the developmental plateau population, and under a written FDA agreement its efficacy is extrapolated to ages 2 to <6, with ASPIRE supplying safety (10-Q). Filters: (1) Female: 1.0, since the pool (May 2023) is female only by construction. (2) MECP2 mutation: 0.918084. In the US Rett Natural History Study, where every participant had complete MECP2 testing, 'A mutation was identified in 95% of 653 females with classic and 73.2% of 112 females with variant RTT' (Percy AK et al., Ann Neurol 2010;68(6):951-5, doi:10.1002/ana.22154, PMID 21104896, PMC3021984 full text). (0.95 x 653 + 0.732 x 112) / 765 = 0.918084. (3) Age 2 and over: 1.0. The median age at diagnosis is 2.7 to 3.8 years (US longitudinal study cited by May 2023), and with carryover a patient diagnosed before 2 ages into the label rather than leaving the pool. (4) Stage: 1.0, since the planned label covers all stages: plateau patients 6 to <22 are studied directly and ages 2 to <6 by extrapolation
eligible_pct.note: JUDGEMENT on the upper age. The label is taken as filed, age 2 and over with no upper limit, although REVEAL studied only up to 21. Itvisma's label runs from age 2 into adulthood, which shows the FDA grants such a label for an intrathecal AAV9. Case for lower: if the FDA limits the label to the studied ages (2 to <22), adults drop out. Those 18 and over are 48.2% of the pool (2,862 / 5,940), so eligible falls to about 0.48 to 0.55. If the label excludes patients with pre-existing anti-AAV9 antibodies, seropositive patients drop out; no such criterion appears in Taysha's filings, and it is not applied. The MECP2 share comes from a clinically confirmed cohort, while the claims pool includes some coded patients without Rett, so the filter is if anything generous. Pool: 5,940 x 0.918084 = 5,453 US patients
eligible_pct.check: Label plan confirmed verbatim in 10-Q 0001193125-26-344610 and 8-K 0001193125-26-344594: ASPIRE supports 'broad labeling of TSHA-102 for patients aged ≥2 years with Rett syndrome', efficacy in ages 2 to <6 'extrapolated from data collected in the REVEAL pivotal trial'. REVEAL entry criteria, as filed: 'females aged 6 to <22 years with Rett syndrome due to MECP2 loss-of-function mutation' in the developmental plateau population. MECP2 share: Percy AK et al., Ann Neurol 2010;68(6):951-5 (PMID 21104896, doi:10.1002/ana.22154, PMC3021984), full text read: 'A mutation was identified in 95% of 653 females with classic and 73.2% of 112 females with variant RTT', and 'All participants had complete mutation testing'. (0.95 x 653 + 0.732 x 112) / 765 = 702.334 / 765 = 0.918084. Median age at diagnosis 2.7 to 3.8 years confirmed in May 2023's discussion. Itvisma's label of '2 years of age and older' with no upper limit is confirmed in the book's labels table, so a no-upper-age AAV9 intrathecal label has precedent. Adults 2,862 / 5,940 = 48.2% confirmed for the case for lower. Not checked: REVEAL's full exclusion list (anti-AAV9 antibody titres, for instance), because Amass TrialCore was out of quota and clinicaltrials.gov cannot be fetched; no such criterion appears in Taysha's filings. Labelled judgement; inputs confirmed.

untreated_carryover_pct.unit: share of untreated eligible patients still eligible the next year
untreated_carryover_pct.source: house rule for a chronic pool that would otherwise outgrow its measured prevalence: retention = pool / (pool + inflow) = 5,940 / (5,940 + 193) = 0.968531, as the remternetug and direclidine seeds set it
untreated_carryover_pct.note: JUDGEMENT. Rett is lifelong, and an untreated patient stays eligible, but the engine has no death exit. With carryover at 1.0, the 193 new patients a year would grow the pool past its measured size, since inflow is 3.2% of prevalence, against 1% for HAE in the NTLA-2002 seed, which kept 1.0. The implied 3.2% annual exit is consistent with a disease that shortens life: survival was 77.8% at 25 years in the Australian cohort (Laurvick 2006, PMID 16615965). At 1.0 the solved penetration is 0.1051 and the peak rises to 515 patients in year 6
untreated_carryover_pct.check: 5,940 / (5,940 + 193) = 0.968531; the same on the eligible basis, 5,453.4 / (5,453.4 + 177.2). The house rule (pool / (pool + inflow)) is the one the brief names. forecast.py derive_new_patients multiplies the unstarted remainder by carryover each year, so the rule gives a 3.15% annual exit. Survival '77.8% at 25 years' confirmed in the Laurvick 2006 abstract (PMID 16615965). At carryover 1.0 re-solved: p = 0.1051, peak 515 in year 6, as stated. The NTLA-2002 seed's 1.0 for HAE is confirmed in its verified file. Labelled judgement.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Incumbent: Daybue (trofinetide, Acadia), the only approved Rett therapy, launched in 2023. 'As of October 2024, over 1,500 individuals in the U.S. have started treatment with DAYBUE' (IRSF, 'DAYBUE in the Real World', rettsyndrome.org/daybue-in-the-real-world/, quoting Acadia; read from the search summary), about 18 months after launch. 1,500 / 5,940 = 25.3% of the diagnosed female pool. Cross-checks, all from search summaries: 954 and 987 unique US patients received a shipment in Q1 and Q2 2025 (Acadia releases), and Acadia described penetration 'in the low 30%' across the Rett community in Q2 2025 (Q2 2025 call), which matches 1,500 over its own 4,500. Solved through the engine (forecast.derive_new_patients: k 1.08, midpoint 2.2, eligible pool 5,453.4, inflow 177.2 a year, carryover 0.968531) so that TSHA-102 has treated 25.3% of its eligible pool, 1,377 patients, by the end of year 5: p = 0.1154. Treated patients run 55, 138, 280, 420 and 483 over 2028-2032, peaking at 483 in 2032, then 478, 445, 407, 370 and 338
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: Daybue's 18-month share of patients started, reached by TSHA-102 in five years. That is a multiple of 1.0 on the share and a slower clock. A one-time irreversible intrathecal gene therapy needs treatment-centre capacity, payer prior authorisation for a $2.59mm course, and caregiver acceptance of a permanent intervention, where Daybue is an oral anyone can stop. Starts are the right analog, not patients on therapy, because a gene therapy patient never discontinues. Case for higher: Daybue's starts kept rising after October 2024, all 12 Part A patients responded, Taysha's market research shows 'strong clinician and caregiver demand' (10-K), and patients who have stopped Daybue are a pool a disease-modifying option can draw from. On Acadia's 'low 30%' share (0.33), p = 0.1557 and the peak is 615 patients, about $1,019mm. Case for lower: the evidence is single-arm, a safety event anywhere in the AAV class would weigh on uptake, stable adults in late stages may not be offered it, and a label capped at under 22 halves the pool. Ten-year cumulative treated: 3,416, 63% of the eligible pool. Implied peak US net revenue is 483 x $1.658mm = about $801mm in 2032, before the royalty netting in economics_share
penetration_peak_pct.check: Anchor confirmed by WebSearch: IRSF 'DAYBUE in the Real World' (rettsyndrome.org/daybue-in-the-real-world/): 'As of October 2024, over 1,500 individuals in the U.S. have started treatment with DAYBUE', per Acadia; Daybue became available 17 April 2023 (Business Wire), so 18 months. Cross-checks confirmed by search: 987 unique US patients shipped in Q2 2025 and FY2025 net sales $391mm (Acadia releases). Not confirmed by me: Acadia's 'low 30%' remark, used only in the case for higher. Recomputed with forecast.py's s_curve and derive_new_patients logic: pool 5,940 x 0.918084 = 5,453.42, inflow 193 x 0.918084 = 177.19, carryover 0.968531, k 1.08, midpoint 2.2; target 1,500 / 5,940 = 25.25% x 5,453.42 = 1,377.1 treated by end of year 5. Bisection gives p = 0.115364, so 0.1154. At 0.1154: 55, 138, 280, 420, 483, 478, 445, 407, 370, 338 over 2028-2037; five-year cumulative 1,377.5; ten-year 3,416 (62.6%); peak 483 x $1.6576mm = $800.9mm. At a 0.33 share, p = 0.1557 and the peak is 615. All match. Labelled judgement: same share, slower clock, with the case each way.

ramp_steepness.source: book: Enhertu's CMS Part B launch fit (864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105, 8,410 beneficiaries 2020-2024; lookup.py demand Enhertu), k = 1.08, midpoint 2.2 years, as carried by the MK-1045 seed (lookup.py seed MK-1045) and reused by the one-time NTLA-2002 and BMS-986353 seeds
ramp_steepness.note: JUDGEMENT to reuse it. The book has no Rett or intrathecal gene therapy launch series, and Daybue's is known only at a single cumulative point. Case for a later midpoint: few centres can dose intrathecally at launch, and each patient needs payer approval for a one-time course
ramp_steepness.check: lookup.py seed MK-1045: ramp_steepness 1.08, 'Enhertu's own launch, fitted: its CMS Part B beneficiaries went 864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105 and 8,410 over 2020 to 2024'; lookup.py demand Enhertu shows those Part B beneficiaries. Reuse in the one-time NTLA-2002 and BMS-986353 seeds confirmed (their verified files carry 1.08 and 2.2, confirmed). No Rett or intrathecal gene therapy launch series exists in the book (lookup.py demand Daybue and Zolgensma return no rows). Labelled judgement.

ramp_midpoint_year.source: as ramp_steepness (Enhertu fit carried in the book)
ramp_midpoint_year.note: Unshifted. The penetration peak was solved on this curve, so the two must move together
ramp_midpoint_year.check: Same Enhertu fit (lookup.py seed MK-1045: ramp_midpoint_year 2.2). s_curve(0) / peak = 1 / (1 + exp(1.08 x 2.2)) = 0.085, the 8.5% year-0 share cited under forecast_start_year. The penetration was solved on this curve, and recomputing it on k 1.08 and midpoint 2.2 reproduces 0.1154.
